subject: Clarifications: delegated on-call admin roles, SCIM deltas & SAML/OIDC attribute mapping
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@cendrix.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@cendrix.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-ups: delegated on-call admins + SCIM/SAML mapping clarifications

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the initial RFP package — the team reviewed and we have a small set of focused clarifications before we finalize the IAM section. High level items:

1) Delegated on-call/admin scoping: can Redwood create time-limited "on-call admin" elevations (30m–8h) scoped to a single customer tenant and limited to a subset of operational actions (restart model endpoint, purge KV cache)? We need the exact controls and evidence (audit log examples).

2) SCIM behaviour for group removals: does Redwood accept PATCH with "remove" operations for group membership sync, or do you require full-group PUT? We need sample payloads and whether you support SCIM change notifications/webhooks for near-real-time updates.

3) SAML/OIDC attribute consumption: for customers using NameID transient and OIDC sub claims, how does Redwood map attributes to internal role assignments? Are there rule-based mappings (e.g., group claim -> role) and precedence rules (SAML assertion vs SCIM provisioning)?

4) Admin immutability/breakglass: can you show how you prevent cross-tenant admin escalation (where an identity with admin role in one tenant cannot accidentally get admin in another)? Also request a runbook or diagram for breakglass and emergency access.

Would you be able to provide short answers and attach sample SCIM payloads and an admin runbook excerpt? We can turn these into a single redline for the RFP.

Thanks — we aim to close IAM by EOD Monday.

—Alice
Alice Monroe
Senior Security Architect, Cendrix Systems

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@cendrix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-ups: delegated on-call admins + SCIM/SAML mapping clarifications

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise responses; attaching artifacts in a follow-up message (SCIM payload samples + runbook extract).

1) Delegated on-call/admin scoping:
- Capability: Yes. Redwood supports tenant-scoped, time-limited elevations tied to a short-lived access token (JWT) and an aud claim bound to the tenant ID. Elevations can be requested via Console or API and are recorded as a discrete event in audit logs.
- Granularity: Actions are policy-driven. We ship a set of fine-grained action scopes (e.g., inference:restart_endpoint, cache:purge_prefix, logs:read_tail). Admin roles can be created as compositions of these scopes.
- Lifecycle: elevation request -> approval (optional auto-approve for on-call) -> token minted (TTL 30m–8h) -> automatic revocation.
- Evidence: audit logs include requestor, approver (if applicable), TTL, bound tenant, and action scopes. Example log line: "2028-03-01T18:00:23Z | event=elevation_granted | actor=alice.cendrix | approver=oncall-bot | tenant=tn-cendrix-01 | scopes=[inference:restart_endpoint,cache:purge_prefix] | token_id=..."

2) SCIM group membership and deltas:
- PATCH support: Redwood accepts SCIM 2.0 PATCH operations for users and groups (operations: add, remove, replace). We do not require PUT for every sync — PATCH is the recommended path for incremental provisioning.
- Change events: Redwood can subscribe to SCIM change notifications via a webhook endpoint (events: User.created/updated/deleted, Group.membership.changed). We also support periodic delta syncs when a webhook is not available.
- Edge cases: when a remove operation removes the last member of a role-mapped group, the role is deactivated for that tenant; we emit a role_deactivated audit event.

3) SAML/OIDC attribute mapping and precedence:
- Mapping: we support declarative mapping rules on the tenant: map SAML attribute or OIDC claim (by name) -> internal role or scope set. Support includes simple mappings (group claim -> role) and regex extraction for attributes.
- NameID / sub handling: if NameID (SAML) or sub (OIDC) is present and the IdP is configured for user provisioning, we prioritize SCIM-provisioned identity-to-role bindings for deterministic membership. If SCIM is not available, attribute-based mappings are applied at login time.
- Precedence: SCIM provisioning (explicit membership) > IdP-provided group/role claims > ad-hoc attribute mappings. We document this precedence and include it in the admin UI.

4) Admin immutability and breakglass:
- Tenant isolation: all admin tokens include the tenant scope; the runtime enforces a tenant-bound check on admin APIs. Cross-tenant elevation is blocked by default.
- Immutable boundaries: role definitions include an immutable flag that prevents assignment outside a specified tenant or namespace. Only Organization Owners can set immutable=true.
- Breakglass: we provide a documented breakglass flow: emergency token generation with multi-party approval (or time-limited auto-approval if org config permits), and immediate audit event + automatic email to security distribution.

Next steps: attaching SCIM payload examples and a short runbook. Marissa / Jonas — please confirm the runbook PDF is the excerpt we want to include in the RFP package.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Security & Trust PM | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@cendrix.com>

Subject: Re: RFP follow-ups: delegated on-call admins + SCIM/SAML mapping clarifications

Kimberly — very helpful, thanks. Couple quick clarifications before we include in the RFP response: 

- For PATCH behaviour: can you include a sample PATCH payload for removing a user from a group (we will test remove-on-absence)? Also include one sample for bulk group membership change (100 users) and how Redwood handles rate-limiting / backpressure.

- For breakglass: can you confirm whether breakglass tokens are stored as reversible or irreversible artifacts in the audit log? We require that any emergency token cannot be replayed after revocation; we also want a sample audit line showing revocation.

If you can drop the artifacts into a single zip or attach inline, we can take them into our procurement packet.

—Alice

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@cendrix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-ups: delegated on-call admins + SCIM/SAML mapping clarifications

Alice — attaching the requested samples and a short runbook excerpt. Key notes inline: 

- SCIM PATCH sample (remove membership): attached file redwood_scim_sample_patch_payloads.json includes a small example and a bulk example using PATCH+Bulk with recommended chunking (100 records per request). We also include a short section on handling 429s: our recommended client strategy is exponential backoff with jitter; the provisioning API returns Retry-After and a reason header.

- Breakglass tokens: tokens are never stored in reversible form. The audit log records token_id and a truncated token fingerprint (sha256 hex prefix) — sufficient to correlate but not to replay. Revocation emits an audit event; example: "2028-03-02T11:58:42Z | event=token_revoked | token_id=tok-89a3 | actor=org-owner-1 | reason=emergency_completion | fingerprint=sha256:3b7f..."

- Attached runbook (delegated_admin_runbook.pdf) contains the on-call approval matrix and sample Slack/Opsgenie webhook configuration for auto-approve. The oncall_role_matrix_v2.png visualizes role-to-scope mappings for the most common operational tasks.

Let us know if you want a short (15 minute) call/demonstration around SCIM delta tests. Happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Attachments: redwood_scim_sample_patch_payloads.json (application/json), delegated_admin_runbook.pdf (application/pdf), oncall_role_matrix_v2.png (image/png)
